text:
Sanjay: quick FYI — after the 18:00 canary push I see a p99 latency regression on a subset of hosts. micro-batch interval set to 1.2ms with jitter 0.5ms. p99 up ~35% on gpt-medium-quant, kv-hit rate fell from ~87% -> ~64%.

Maria: can you paste the short logs/selection traces? curious if kernel selection drifted or if batches are starving KV priming.

Sanjay: excerpt from host-42 around the spike: 
```
[2026-03-17T18:02:13Z] incoming req seq_len=34 selected kernel=fast_attn_v2 (prefers kv-prefix)
[2026-03-17T18:02:14Z] batch formed size=5 token_budget_target=512 observed_tokens=420 -> kernel fallback=matmul_approx
[2026-03-17T18:02:14Z] kv_cache_hit=false (cold), latency tok=0.98ms, total=12.4ms
```
looks like we frequently fail to meet the budget and choose fallback kernels that don't leverage our optimized KV path.

Kevin: that matches a hypothesis: if coalesce delay + jitter reduces observed batch tokens we might hit a lower kernel selection tier. fallback kernels have worse latency for short seqs. we should try tuning holdtime (micro-batch interval) and token_budget_target together.

Ashley: ran a 30m canary across 10 hosts with current params, pulled perf summary (via PerfBot):

PerfBot: 
- hosts: 10 canary
- workload: prod-like replay (60rps, 10% long tail seqs)
- p50: 6.1ms (no change)
- p95: 18.2ms (+9%)
- p99: 52.1ms (+35%)
- throughput: 12.6k tokens/s (down 7%)
- kv_hit_rate: 64% (was 87%)
- token_budget_achieved_ratio: 0.82
- kernel_mix: fast_attn_v2 48%, matmul_approx 39%, others 13%

PerfBot: note -> kernel_mix drift correlates with lower token_budget_achieved_ratio.

Lee: proposed next steps: 1) quick A/B: increase token_budget_target to 640 and holdtime_ms to 2.0ms on 20% hosts, 2) add a short window metric kv_hit_by_kernel and token_budget_achieved_ratio per host, 3) if A/B fails, revert to previous holdtime/jitter and roll forward diagnostic flags.

Maria: +1 on metrics. also add a histogram of batch_formed_tokens so we can see distribution, not just mean.

Sanjay: config snippet I propose applying to canary group (low-risk):
```json
{"microbatch": {"holdtime_ms": 2.0, "jitter_ms": 0.3, "coalesce_max_tokens": 2048}, "batching": {"token_budget_target": 640, "min_batch_size": 2}}
```
this keeps coalesce window small but increases budget target so kernel selector stays in fast_attn path.

Kevin: I'm starting the A/B now. command: `./deploy/canary_ctl --group ab_test_token_budget --pct 20 --param microbatch.holdtime_ms=2.0 --param microbatch.jitter_ms=0.3 --param batching.token_budget_target=640`

Kevin: quick heads-up — initial 5m looks promising: p99 down to +8% (was +35), kv_hit ~82%, token_budget_achieved_ratio ~0.95. will continue 30m run and post full numbers.

PerfBot: interim A/B snapshot (after 10m)
- control p99: 51.8ms
- variant p99: 21.4ms
- kv_hit control: 63% variant: 82%
- token_budget_achieved control: 0.81 variant: 0.95

Ashley: awesome — if stable, we should consider making this the default tuning for similar traffic profiles. Also add a guard: if token_budget_achieved_ratio < 0.85 trigger a fallback to safe parameters automatically. :robot_face:

Lee: will open a short RFC to document rationale + rollout steps. cc @maria for metrics dashboard widgets.

Sanjay: thanks all — @kevin let me know end-of-run numbers and then either promote or rollback. filing a follow-up note in eng-runtime/experiment-tracker.

Maria: minor nit — also verify kernel-selector thresholds for long sequences; we saw a couple of fallbacks triggered for seq>512 in the logs. maybe adjust sequence cutoff mapping for fast_attn_v2.

Kevin: noted. adding a probe to log kernel_selector_reason on the next canary sweep.

Ashley: tagging incident if regression returns after rollout. otherwise i'll draft a short postmortem-style runbook for this tuning change. :memo:
